Yarrells School & Nursery
Welcome to
Welcome to Yarrells School and Nursery, an independent day school and nursery in Poole, Dorset for boys and girls aged 6 months to 11 years. Set within beautiful grounds near Poole Harbour, Yarrells provides a nurturing environment where children develop confidence, curiosity and a lifelong love of learning. With small class sizes, dedicated teachers and a rich curriculum including sport, creative arts and outdoor learning, every child is encouraged to discover their talents and reach their full potential.
Independent Prep School and Nursery in Poole, Dorset
The Yarrells Learning Journey
A Country School in an Urban Area
Nestled near Poole Harbour, Yarrells School & Nursery is a thriving family school set within six acres of beautiful grounds where the charm of a traditional country school meets the convenience of an urban setting. Founded in 1927 as St Monica’s School, Yarrells offers a unique learning environment with excellent facilities and space for children to learn, explore and thrive.

Yarrells' New Baby Unit Officially Opens Its Doors Next Month
Yarrells is delighted to announce that our brand new Baby Unit will officially open its doors next month, following the receipt of our Certificate of Registration from Ofsted.
This is a significant milestone for the Yarrells Nursery, marking the moment we extend our care and provision to our very youngest children, welcoming babies from just six months old into Greenwood, our award-winning Early Years building set among the woodland of our Upton estate.
The Baby Unit has been carefully designed with the needs of babies in mind, offering a nurturing, stimulating and safe environment in which they can explore, develop and thrive under the care of our dedicated early years team. Every detail, from the layout of the rooms to the daily routines, has been thoughtfully planned to support the very earliest stages of a child's development.
Receiving our Certificate of Registration from Ofsted confirms that the Baby Unit meets the rigorous standards required to care for babies and young children, and we are incredibly proud of the work that has gone into reaching this point.
For families who have been waiting for this moment, places in the new Baby Unit are now available. We would love to welcome your baby into the Yarrells family.
To find out more, or to arrange a visit, please contact us at admissions@yarrells.co.uk or call 01202 622229.
Say hello to our brand new Baby Unit, opening next month inside Greenwood! After receiving our Certificate of Registration from Ofsted, we are so excited to welcome babies from just 6 months old into this beautiful space.
Spaces are limited, get in touch to find out more.

The introduction of the new baby unit is seen as a fitting start to the next century of the school's history.
The Greenwood building has been a home for learning for thousands of children over the past decade, providing experiences in woodland trails, a kitchen garden, and wildlife watching.

Extra-Curricular Clubs
Before school, after school, and everything in between.
At Yarrells, the day doesn't begin and end with the bell. We offer a rich programme of before and after-school clubs, wrap-around care from 7:30am to 5:45pm, and a wide variety of activities that change every half term — giving every child the chance to discover a new passion.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club — 7:30am to 8:00am
Our Breakfast Club is the perfect start to the day — children are welcomed in, settled, and fuelled up ready to learn.
This service is available at an additional cost of £9 per session, which is itemised on our schedule of fees.
Early Birds
Early Birds — 8:00am to 8:30am
Early Birds is a free supervised session available to all pupils from Reception to Year 6. A relaxed and friendly start to the school day.
No booking required, no additional charge.
After-School Clubs
We run an extensive programme of after-school clubs between 3:45pm and 5:30pm, changing on a half-termly basis to keep things fresh and exciting. Clubs span sport, arts, music, languages, and more, there is genuinely something for everyone.
The full programme of clubs is sent to all parents at the start of the preceding term. Places are allocated thoughtfully so that every child has the opportunity to engage in a wide range of activities across the year.
After-School Care
Free After-School Care — 3:30pm to 4:30pm
If your child is not in a club but you need them to stay on at school, our free after-school care session runs until 4:30pm every day, providing safe, supervised, and friendly care at no additional cost.
Any Questions About Clubs or Care?
Our school office team is always happy to help with questions about our clubs programme or wrap-around care arrangements. Get in touch and we'll be happy to help.

pageCache.text:
English at Yarrells
Language is at the very heart of children's development. At Yarrells, we nurture a genuine love of reading and writing that lasts long beyond our pupils' years at school.
Words that open worlds.
Language is at the very heart of children’s development: it enables them to formulate and express their thoughts, to explain themselves and communicate with others, to organise their thinking, and to interpret their experiences and make sense of the world around them.
The aim of the English Department throughout the school is to develop pupils’ abilities to communicate with others as effectively as possible in both speech and writing, and to have confidence in their skills. Critically, we wish to give pupils a love of language, both written and spoken, which will last beyond their years at school; to encourage pupils to read and write for pleasure and to appreciate literature in all its forms; and to develop their own creativity.
The study and development of skills in English are not, of course, confined to the formal teaching of the subject. English is both a tool and a medium for all learning in school and for life outside the classroom.

pageCache.text:
The History of Yarrells
From its founding as St Monica's in Deal, Kent in 1927, to its home in Upton, Poole, and its approach to its centenary in 2027.
Nearly a century of care, continuity and community.
Founded in 1927, Yarrells has been nurturing children and supporting families for almost 100 years. As we approach our centenary in 2027, we look back with pride at the journey that has shaped who we are today.
1927 — St Monica's, Deal, Kent
Founded by Miss M E Clark, who served as both Proprietor and Headmistress from the school's very beginning. The school that would one day become Yarrells opened its doors for the first time.
1940 — St Monica's moves to Poole, Dorset
During the Second World War, the school relocated from Deal in Kent to Poole, Dorset, establishing roots in the community it has called home ever since. Miss Clark continued as Headmistress and Proprietor.
1957 — New leadership at St Monica's
Miss G W Jeanes joined as Headmistress, with Miss Jeanes and Mrs P B Badham taking joint ownership of the school as Proprietors.
1989 — The Covell family arrives
Mrs Natalie A Covell joined St Monica's as Headmistress, the beginning of the family's long and lasting connection to the school, while Miss Jeanes and Mrs Badham remained as Proprietors.
1992 — Yarrells Preparatory School is born
St Monica's was renamed Yarrells Preparatory School. Mr and Mrs Anthony M Covell became Proprietors, establishing the family-run model that defines the school to this day. The school's name was inspired by 19th-century naturalist William Yarrell, reflecting the school's spirit of curiosity, a love of the natural world, and learning beyond the classroom.
2004 — Mrs Natalie Covell becomes Head
Mrs Natalie A Covell took on the role of Headmistress, Proprietor and Director, leading the school with warmth, ambition and a deep commitment to every child in her care.
2013 — Mrs Charlotte Oosthuizen appointed Head
Mrs Charlotte Oosthuizen joined as Headmistress, with Mrs Natalie A Covell continuing as Proprietor and Director.
2016 — Mr Andrew Roberts-Wray appointed Head
Mr Andrew Roberts-Wray joined as Headmaster, with Mrs Natalie A Covell continuing as Proprietor and Director
2017 — Mrs Linda Sharpe, Acting Headteacher
Mrs Linda Sharpe served as Acting Headteacher during this period of transition, with Mrs Natalie A Covell continuing as Proprietor and Director.
2018 — Mrs Sally Moulton appointed Head
Mrs Sally Moulton joined as Head, with Mrs Natalie A Covell continuing as Proprietor and Director.
2024 — Mrs Clare Cunningham appointed Headmistress
Mrs Clare Cunningham, part of the Yarrells community for over 20 years, former Deputy Head, SENDCo and Yarrells parent, was appointed Headmistress. Mrs Natalie A Covell continues as Proprietor and Director, now supported by her sons Mr Adam Covell and Mr Crispian Covell as Directors.
2027 — Centenary
Yarrells approaches its 100th anniversary, a milestone that reflects nearly a century of family ownership, community spirit, and a genuine commitment to giving every child the brightest of beginnings.

Inspection Reports
Yarrells School and Nursery is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) on behalf of the Department for Education. ISI inspections assess the quality of pupils' academic and personal development, the effectiveness of the school's leadership and management, and compliance with independent school standards.
ISI Inspection 2025 — Significant Strength
In October 2025, Yarrells was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate. Following the inspection, the school was awarded an ISI Significant Strength, the highest commendation the ISI can grant. This places Yarrells among only a small number of schools nationally to have received this recognition.
The Significant Strength was awarded in recognition of the exceptional depth of learning demonstrated by pupils across the school.
Inspectors noted that pupils engage with their learning with genuine curiosity and enthusiasm, and that the school's approach to developing confident, well-rounded individuals is reflected clearly in the outcomes for children at every stage.
What is the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI)?
An ISI Significant Strength is awarded when inspectors identify a particular area of exceptional practice that goes beyond the standard inspection framework. It is distinct from — and rarer than — an overall 'Excellent' grading. Schools can receive an Excellent rating without being awarded a Significant Strength. The commendation is reserved for schools demonstrating genuinely outstanding provision in a specific area.
What inspectors found at Yarrells
The 2025 inspection highlighted a number of strengths across the school:
Pupils demonstrate an exceptional depth of learning and a genuine love of discovery
Children are confident, articulate and engaged — both in and beyond the classroom
The school's nurturing environment enables every child to develop at their own pace
Leadership and management were found to be effective, with a clear and purposeful vision
The school meets all requirements of the independent school standards
What inspectors found at Yarrells
Mrs Clare Cunningham, Headmistress of Yarrells, reflected on the inspection outcome:
"We are incredibly proud of this recognition. The Significant Strength commendation is a reflection of the work of every member of our team, and above all of the children themselves, who bring such enthusiasm and depth to their learning every single day. At Yarrells, we believe that truly knowing every child is the foundation of exceptional education, and it is deeply gratifying to see that belief validated by our inspectors."

pageCache.text:
Why a Standalone Prep School Still Matters: What Parents in Dorset Should Know
Across the UK, the independent school landscape is shifting. Financial pressures and policy changes have prompted many schools to merge, join larger education groups, or restructure entirely. For parents navigating school choices, this raises a timely question: what is the real value of a school that remains truly independent?
At Yarrells School & Nursery, we believe the answer lies in something that can't be replicated by a larger group structure: the freedom to put every decision at the service of your child.
Freedom to Focus Entirely on Children
One of the defining strengths of a standalone prep school is its ability to remain completely focused on the needs of its pupils. Without the influence of a wider group structure, independent prep schools have the freedom to build everything around the children in front of them, from how the school day is structured to how pastoral care is delivered and what enrichment looks like in practice.
At Yarrells, that community is our boys and girls aged 6 months to 11 years, right here in Poole, Dorset. Every decision we make, from timetabling to enrichment to pastoral care, is made for them, not for a board of trustees elsewhere.
Agility to Adapt and Innovate
Standalone schools can adapt quickly, introduce new initiatives and ensure that learning experiences remain tailored to the age group they specialise in. This year alone, Yarrells has opened a new dedicated baby room, expanded its outdoor learning programme, and been recognised by ISI inspectors with a Significant Strength commendation, one of the most meaningful recognitions an independent school can receive during an ISI inspection, for the exceptional depth of learning demonstrated by its pupils.
A School That Knows Every Child
Small class sizes and a close-knit community mean that at Yarrells, no child is ever just a number. Parents tell us again and again that what sets us apart is the sense that their child is truly seen.
As one Yarrells parent put it: "It genuinely feels like leaving our child with family."
That depth of relationship, between teachers, children and families, is only possible when a school is free to build its own culture from the ground up, without pressure to conform to a wider group's identity or priorities.
Continuity and Stability
Approaching its 100th anniversary, Yarrells has been family-owned and community-rooted since 1927. That continuity matters. Parents choosing a prep school aren't just choosing a curriculum, they're choosing a community, a set of values, and a team of people who will walk alongside their family for years.
Choosing the Right Fit
When finalising this important choice, it can be helpful to isolate the factors that matter most to you and find a learning environment that offers the best fit for your child. For many families in the Poole and Dorset area, that fit is Yarrells, a school where confidence, curiosity and a lifelong love of learning are nurtured every single day, set within six beautiful acres near Poole Harbour.

pageCache.pageTitle: Yarrells Nursery | Poole, Dorset | Children from 6 Months to 4 Years — Yarrells School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Nestled in beautiful woodland grounds, a warm, magical place where curiosity blooms and every child feels truly at home.
Yarrells Nursery
Where little oneslove to learn
Tucked into a snug corner of our beautiful woodland estate in Poole, Dorset, Greenwood is purpose-built and thoughtfully designed for our youngest learners. It's calm, inspiring, and completely secure.
Led by an experienced, qualified teacher, our Nursery is fully aligned with the main school's high expectations, so children benefit from the entire Yarrells community from day one.
From forest adventures to swimming lessons, from French to cookery, the opportunities here are truly exceptional for such young children.
Our magical Greenwood setting
Our Nursery Groups
Each group is thoughtfully designed for its age range, with the right balance of learning, play, and care.
Cottontails (Pips)
6 MONTHS - 18 MONTHS
A nurturing, home-from-home environment for your baby's earliest months. We follow your baby's own routine, supporting their development through songs, stories, and sensory play, all year round.
Session times8:00am – 3:30pm 8:00am – 6:00pmAll-year-round only
Kittens
A nurturing, home-from-home environment that encourages curiosity and independence. We support your toddler's growing confidence through active play, early language, and social experiences, all year round.
Session times8:00am – 3:30pm 8:00am – 6:00pmAll-year-round only
Nutkins
From the age of 2, children join our lively Nutkins group. Days are filled with Forest School, music, PE, outdoor play, and hands-on discovery — with wraparound care available from 7:30am to 6:00pm.
Session times7:30am – 6:00pm (flexible)Term-time or all-year-round
Squirrels
In Squirrels, children flourish with specialist French and swimming lessons alongside a rich play-based curriculum. The perfect preparation for a smooth, confident step up to Reception.
Session times7:30am – 6:00pm (flexible)Term-time or all-year-round
What every child benefits from
From 2 years, all nursery children access these exceptional facilities and opportunities
Swimming Pool (Squirrels)
A seamless step up to Reception
Moving from Nursery to Reception at Yarrells is an exciting, smooth journey, not a big leap. Children already know the building, the staff, and the routines. They're ready.
Each Nursery child is paired with a senior school "buddy", sharing reading, play, and special moments that build real connections across the school.
Moving from Yarrells Nursery to Reception is an exciting and smooth step for children!
Here’s what makes the transition special:
Familiar Environment - Children already know the layout, staff, and routines.
Consistent Learning - Nursery and Reception share the same nurturing educational approach.
Social Support - Children build on friendships with familiar faces.
Tailored Support - Reception teachers prepare children with structured guidance.
Developmental Continuity - A play-based approach helps children grow academically and creatively.
Holistic Growth - Focusing on emotional resilience, independence, and communication.
Encouragement of Independence - Gaining confidence to take on new challenges.
Fostering a Love of Learning - Nurturing curiosity and a passion for discovery.
The move from Nursery to Reception at Yarrells ensures a seamless, supportive, and joyful learning journey!
Come and see Greenwood for yourself
Choosing the right nursery is one of the most important decisions you'll make.
We warmly welcome families to visit, meet our team, and see the magic for themselves.
admissions@yarrells.co.uk

Why funding applies between 11:00am–5:00pm
As a school-based nursery, we're able to offer children extra enrichment activities such as Forest School, Swimming, Dance, Drama and French, that go beyond what government funding covers. Because these sit outside the scope of funded childcare, we run them between 8:00am and 11:00am, so every nursery child benefits from them as part of their day.
Government funding (set by Dorset Council) then applies from 11:00am–5:00pm (up to 6 hours per day), covering core nursery education and care, with optional extras such as hot lunch and consumables available at an additional cost during this time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Open Day at Yarrells — Yarrells School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Open Mornings at Yarrells
Discover the Magic of Yarrells
Join us for an Open Morning and see for yourself why families choose Yarrells, where every child is inspired to love learning in a warm, nature-rich community.
A Morning that Changes Everything
Our Open Mornings are more than just a tour — they are an invitation to experience Yarrells alive. Watch children engrossed in forest school, hear laughter from the performing arts hall, and feel the warmth of a genuine community that puts every child at its heart.
Whether you are considering our Nursery for your youngest or our Prep School for an older child, we welcome you and your family to walk through our doors and see how we inspire a love of learning every single day.
OPEN DAYFriday 18th SeptemberBOOK HERE
Yarrells House, Upton,Poole, Dorset BH16 5EU
9:00am to 1:00pmBy appointment only
What to Expect
01
A Warm Welcome
You will be greeted personally by our Head, Mrs Clare Cunningham, and our admissions team — who are on hand to answer every question, large or small.
02
A Guided School Tour
Explore our beautiful Dorset grounds, classrooms, Forest School, performing arts spaces, sports facilities, and the newly opened Greenwood Early Years Building.
03
Children in Action
Our mornings are held during school time so you can watch real lessons and experience the energy, creativity, and joy that define a typical day at Yarrells.
04
Meet the Community
Speak with current parents and pupils who can share first-hand what makes Yarrells such a special place — honest, warm, and completely genuine.
05
Admissions Guidance
Our team will walk you through the application process, fees, nursery sessions, early years funding, and any bespoke support your child may need.
06
Time to Decide, Gently
There is no pressure and no sales pitch. Our Open Morning is simply an opportunity for you and your child to feel whether Yarrells is the right fit.
A School Like No Other
Yarrells is a small school with a very big heart. Rated outstanding by ISI inspectors and listed in The Good Schools Guide, we offer something increasingly rare: a place where children are genuinely known, deeply nurtured, and inspired to become the very best version of themselves.
Exceptional Teaching
Our ISI inspection recognised a "significant strength in depth of knowledge and understanding" across the school. Every lesson is crafted to spark genuine curiosity and a love of learning that lasts a lifetime.
Wellbeing at the Centre
Pupils show confidence, empathy and strong emotional awareness. Wellbeing is a shared priority at Yarrells, with our core values woven into school life from the earliest years, not just a policy, but a practice.
Nature-Rich Learning
Set in beautiful Dorset grounds, our Forest School and outdoor learning provision give children regular, meaningful time in nature, building resilience, creativity and connection to the world around them.
Rich, Broad Curriculum
From tennis and swimming to performing arts, STEM, and eco school, every child finds their passion at Yarrells. Our curriculum nurtures independence, curiosity and the confidence to present ideas with flair.
A Genuine Community
Yarrells is a family community in the truest sense. Our PTA, parent events, and open-door ethos mean you are not just choosing a school, you are joining a group of people who genuinely care about each other.
Small School, Big Futures
Our size is our strength. Every teacher knows every child. Pupils leave Yarrells for leading senior schools across Dorset and beyond, confident, authentic learners ready for whatever comes next.
“Yarrells is a gorgeous school, full of happy children who love to learn. Our relationships with the young people we teach are so important, we work really hard to foster happiness, self-confidence and aspiration for life in every individual here.”
Mrs Clare Cunningham · Head, Yarrells School & Nursery
Book Your Visit
Places at our Open Mornings are offered by appointment only. Complete the form below and our Admissions Registrar, Kristal Bowdler, will email you confirming the booking. We look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Call us: 01202 622229
Email: admissions@yarrells.co.uk
Yarrells House, Upton, Poole, Dorset BH16 5EU
